title: Local closed-fibre criterion when the source completion map is regular
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ and $(S,\mathfrak n)$ be commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $f:R\to S$ be a local ring homomorphism, meaning $f(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$ and $\widehat R=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R/\mathfrak m^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Assume the canonical map $R\to\widehat R$ is regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Then $f$ is regular if and only if it is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $S/\mathfrak mS$ is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Here geometrically regular means Noetherian and remaining regular after every finite purely inseparable extension of $k$, and regular ring means Noetherian with regular local rings at every prime. No completeness or finite-type assumption on $R$ or $S$ is imposed.

proof.text: If $f$ is regular, [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] gives flatness and geometric regularity of its fibre at $\mathfrak m$. The residue field there is $k$. The canonical identification $S\otimes_R k\cong S/\mathfrak mS$ sends $s\otimes\bar r$ to the class of $sf(r)$, with inverse $\bar s\mapsto s\otimes1$: changing $s$ by a sum of $f(a)t$, $a\in\mathfrak m$, changes the latter by zero. Thus the closed fibre has exactly the required $k$-algebra structure.

Conversely suppose $f$ is flat and $\overline S=S/\mathfrak mS$ is geometrically regular over $k$. Locality gives $\mathfrak mS\subseteq\mathfrak n$, so [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure] makes $\overline S$ a nonzero local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak mS$. It is Noetherian by its assumed geometric regularity. Apply [lem-sfb-geometrically-regular-local-field-adic-smooth] to this $k$-algebra. Then [lem-weil-pbc-flat-formally-smooth-closed-fibre-adic], using the assumed flatness of $f$, makes $S$ formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.

source.place: Tags 07EL, theorem-regular-fs, (1) implies (2); 07NQ, proposition-fs-flat-fibre-fs, (2) implies (3), as used in 0H7U.

proof.text: Put $\widehat S=\varprojlim_jS/\mathfrak n^j$ and let $\widehat f:\widehat R\to\widehat S$ be the map induced by $f$ on quotient levels, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-complete-source-target]. Both completions are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], local with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m\widehat R$ and $\mathfrak n\widehat S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], and complete by [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] applied to each ring as its own module. The ideals are finitely generated since the original rings are Noetherian. The extended-ideal powers are $\mathfrak m^j\widehat R$ and $\mathfrak n^j\widehat S$, so this is also completeness for their maximal ideals. The induced map is local: it sends each generator from $\mathfrak m$ into $\mathfrak n\widehat S$, and hence sends $\mathfrak m\widehat R$ into that maximal ideal. The same completion lemma makes $\widehat f$ formally smooth for the $\mathfrak n\widehat S$-adic topology.

source.place: Tag 07ED, lemma-formally-smooth-completion, (1) implies (3); completion structure: Algebra Tags 0316, 05GI and 05GG.

proof.text: The local homomorphism $\widehat f$ is now between complete Noetherian local rings and is formally smooth for the target maximal-ideal-adic topology. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-complete-local-regular] proves that $\widehat f$ is regular.

source.place: Tag 07PM, proposition-fs-regular, (4) implies (1), as used in 0H7U.

proof.text: The canonical map $c_R:R\to\widehat R$ is regular by hypothesis. Check the extra hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition]: for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the fibre $\widehat S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the quotient by $\mathfrak p$ of the localization of $\widehat S$ at the image of $R\setminus\mathfrak p$. Writing $h=\widehat f c_R$, the identification sends $s\otimes(\bar a/\bar b)$ to $sh(a)/h(b)$ modulo $\mathfrak p$, with inverse $s/h(b)\mapsto s\otimes1/\bar b$. This localization is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]; its quotient is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. Hence regular composition gives $\widehat f c_R:R\to\widehat S$ regular.

source.place: Tag 07QI, lemma-regular-composition, used in the proof of 0H7U; Algebra Tag 00FN for Noetherian fibres.

proof.text: Let $c_S:S\to\widehat S$ be the completion map. On every quotient level both $c_Sf$ and $\widehat f c_R$ send $r$ to the class of $f(r)$, so these maps agree. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], $c_S$ is flat and induces a surjection on spectra. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-permanence] to $R\xrightarrow f S\xrightarrow{c_S}\widehat S$ and the regular composite from Step 5. It follows that $f$ is regular, proving the converse.
